title: reading notes: llm inference optimizations and iclr takeaways
content:
Quick notes + action items from reading / ICML/ICLR-ish papers and internal discussion (mostly for my own memory; rough).

Context / goal:
- Trying to collect practical ideas we can evaluate in Redwood serving runtime: reduce p99 for short-chat workloads, reduce per-token GPU cost for high-throughput embedding/summary pipelines, and make model fallbacks cheaper.
- Focus areas: KV cache management, continuous/elastic batching, quantization-aware kernel selection, and rollout strategies that keep quality regressions visible.

Papers / blog summaries (sketches):
1) "Adaptive KV-cache sharding for multi-session inference" (arXiv:2501.01234)
- Idea: shard KV cache across GPU-local caches with lightweight directory mapping on CPU so hot prefixes don't force cross-GPU fetches.
- Results: 20-35% p99 improvement for multi-session short-turn chats; slight throughput hit for long-context (because of directory overhead).
- Practical notes: requires a directory service and quick LRU/TTL heuristics per shard. Might integrate with our routing layer to bias requests to GPU owning the cache.
- Questions: how to measure "hot prefix" reliably in streaming setting? cost of directory lookups vs remote memcpy?

2) "Continuous batching with latency SLOs" (company blog + ICLR talk)
- Idea: maintain open micro-batch windows per GPU and close them based on latency budget + current batch size distribution. Use per-route latency budget to decide per-request batching policy.
- Results: better average utilization while keeping percentiles bounded. Works best when request size distribution is skewed (many short requests).
- Practical notes: aligns with Redwood Optimize recommendations (we can expose per-route SLOs and autoscale batch windows). Integration points: runtime batching loop + console policy UI + cost modeling.

3) "Quantization-aware kernel selection for sequence-dep models" (arXiv:2408.06789)
- Idea: pick different kernels for q4/q8/float paths depending on length and attention pattern; fallback to higher-precision kernels for head tokens where quality matters.
- Results: 10-25% cost reduction for generation apps with minimal quality loss if head tokens use higher precision.
- Practical notes: we already have kernel registry; need to add heuristics to pick per-token/per-layer kernels and a way to measure quality drop with AB tests.

ICLR/Conference takeaways (short):
- Lots of talk about holistic inference stacks (model + compiler + runtime). Opportunity: emphasize our unified runtime + routing as differentiator.
- More reproducible perf benchmarks being published (good for our benchmark suite).
- Emerging evals focusing on safety/regression detection at deploy time — tie into our rollout & eval pipeline.

Personal experiments / ideas to try (priority order):
1) Prototype a cheap "hot-prefix detector" in the runtime: sliding window token fingerprint counts (bloom-like) to mark prefixes as hot and pin to a shard. Measure false positives and mem overhead. (Owner: Ryan)
2) Add per-route micro-batching budget knobs in Dedicated config + expose in Console as "latency SLO (ms)". Run AB on canary traffic to evaluate cost/quality tradeoffs. (Owner: Noah/Console)
3) Add a small kernel-selection shim: annotate model runtime with layer-level heuristics to pick q4 vs float for first N tokens. Run offline eval on internal prompts. (Owner: SRE/Serving)
4) Add an eval to Redwood Optimize that measures head-token perplexity drift when applying quantization kernels.

Open questions / risks:
- Complexity vs benefit: hot-shard directory and per-token kernel selection add operational complexity; need rollout & fallback policies.
- Measurement: we need stable short-request perf harness (SLO-bench) to measure p50/p95/p99 without noise from autoscaling.
- Backwards compatibility: customer pinned model versions — ensure changes are opt-in or behind flags.

Notes to self / next steps:
- Draft proposal for hot-prefix sharding (1 page): include cost model (mem + directory lookups) and an experiment plan. Add RFC link to REINF-221.
- Sync with Console folks about showing per-route latency SLOs (quick sync with Sophie).
- Run offline quantization head-token eval on 3 small models (gpt-like 1.5B, 6B) this sprint.

Quick links referenced: 
- arXiv adaptive KV-cache: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.01234
- quantization-aware kernels: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.06789
- internal PR prototype (runtime batching): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/412

Rough risk/impact table (notes):
- Hot-prefix sharding: impact=high (p99 up), risk=medium (ops complexity)
- Continuous batching tweaks: impact=medium (cost up to 15% savings), risk=low (config-only)
- Per-token kernel selection: impact=medium-high (cost savings + quality risk), risk=medium-high

Tags for search: kv cache, batching, quantization, rollout, evals

-- end of notes --

(If anyone reads this and wants to join experiments ping me; keeping this in Drive as scratch doc while I turn into a short RFC.)
